framework.name: Gin
framework.tagline: A fast, minimal HTTP web framework for Go.
framework.overview: Gin wraps net/http with a radix-tree router, middleware chain, and ergonomic JSON binding/validation. Master it by starting with a JSON endpoint, then params, middleware, request binding with validation, route groups, and centralized error handling.

challenges.title: 1. Router and JSON response
challenges.concept: `gin.Default()` gives an engine with logger + recovery middleware. Handlers receive a `*gin.Context`; `c.JSON` writes a status code and marshals a body.
hints: gin.H is a shortcut for map[string]any.

challenges.title: 2. Path and query params
challenges.concept: Path segments use `:name` and are read with `c.Param`. Query string values use `c.Query` / `c.DefaultQuery`.
challenges.goal: GET /users/:id?verbose=true echoes both values as JSON.
steps: Return both in a JSON object.

challenges.title: 3. Custom middleware
challenges.concept: Middleware is a `gin.HandlerFunc` that runs around handlers. Call `c.Next()` to continue the chain; set values with `c.Set` and abort with `c.AbortWithStatus`.
challenges.goal: Write a middleware that stores a request id and continues the chain.
steps: Read it back in a handler with c.GetString.

challenges.title: 4. Bind and validate JSON
challenges.concept: `c.ShouldBindJSON` decodes the body into a struct and runs `binding` validation tags. On failure it returns an error you translate into a 400.
challenges.goal: POST /users validates {name required, email must be an email}.
steps: Add binding tags: binding:"required" and binding:"required,email".
Return 400 on error, 201 with the body on success.
hints: json tags name the fields; binding tags validate them.
c.ShouldBindJSON returns an error to check.

challenges.title: 5. Versioned route groups
challenges.concept: `r.Group` shares a path prefix and middleware across related routes, so you can version an API or guard a subtree cleanly.
challenges.goal: Expose GET /api/v1/health under a versioned group.
hints: Groups can be nested and take their own .Use().
The prefix is prepended to every child route.

challenges.title: 6. Centralized error handling
challenges.concept: Handlers can attach errors with `c.Error(err)` and abort; a trailing middleware inspects `c.Errors` after `c.Next()` and renders one consistent error response.
challenges.goal: Attach an error in a handler and render it from an error middleware.
steps: Write middleware that calls c.Next() then checks c.Errors.
If any error exists, write a JSON 500 with the last error.
In the handler, call c.Error(err) and c.Abort().
hints: c.Errors.Last() gives the most recent error.
Register the error middleware first with r.Use.
